title: Floor Thirteen
character: a woman in her late twenties with dark wavy shoulder-length hair, wearing a fitted charcoal blazer over a white blouse
style: cinematic semi-realistic digital painting, moody film lighting, rich shadows, subtle film grain

lines.say: I work nights on the forty-first floor. Nobody else is up here after two.
lines.scene: the narrator alone at a desk in a dark open-plan office high in a skyscraper, one desk lamp on, Chicago skyline lights through tall windows, wide shot

lines.say: Tonight the elevator opened on its own, and one button was glowing. Thirteen.
lines.scene: the narrator standing in front of open brass elevator doors in a dark hallway, warm light spilling out, a single glowing button on the panel, medium shot

lines.say: This building has no thirteenth floor. They skipped it when it was built.
lines.scene: close-up of an elevator button panel with brass buttons, the narrator's hand hovering near one softly glowing blank button, shallow depth of field

lines.say: I stepped in anyway. The doors closed, and the music stopped.
lines.scene: inside an old brass-lined elevator, the narrator's tense reflection in the polished doors, light flickering overhead, low angle

lines.say: They opened on a hallway lit by candles. Every door had my name on it.
lines.scene: a long old-fashioned hotel hallway lit only by candles in wall sconces, dozens of identical wooden doors, the narrator seen from behind at the entrance, symmetrical composition

lines.say: Then a phone started ringing behind the first door.
lines.scene: the narrator's hand reaching for an antique brass doorknob, thin warm light under the door, candlelight, dramatic close-up

question: Would you open that door? Yes, or no?
